trust_decision.summary: Whether a state-changing backend custom action (?do=X&key=Y) was really requested by the logged-in user is decided only by RequestTokenListener for POST requests; the key= dispatcher in Backend::getBackendModule and the DC_Table/DC_Folder GET-token checks (which key on act=, not key=) never check the token, so each GET custom action has to check rt itself.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'custom backend actions'; that is the key= custom-action dispatcher, which calls the configured callback with no token check.

DI wiring of DebugController (token manager + token name)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: manager-bundle/src/EventListener/BackendMenuListener.php:70-74 (link producer that must carry rt, otherwise the protected DebugController action breaks); the DebugController itself sits in manager-bundle, a different package from the core key= dispatcher

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The debug toggle lives in manager-bundle and only flips a dev cookie for admins, so a solver focused on tl_opt_in 'resend' (a DCA operation) could treat it as a separate, harmless developer feature; likewise newsletter 'block' sits in another bundle and already has a JS confirm() prompt.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Read-only or form-showing key= actions (key=compare, key=exportTheme, key=new_tpl, key=importTheme, key=import, the CSV wizard keys) are reached by GET links without rt (global ops) or with forms that POST later; a central rt check in the dispatcher at Backend.php:324 would break them. Separately, the debug toggle link must have rt added or enable/disable stops working.
